title: I Let the Community-Radio Board Hours Catch the DJ Who Never Signed Off

parts.text: I was slated 4:00–6:00 p.m. and at 4:07 DJ Rex was still live with no sign-off in the log. The wall said: SIGN ON. SIGN OFF. BOARD FOLLOWS THE LOG. I was twenty-six, volunteer DJ, holding a program sheet. Rex kept talking. "Personalities are the board." I photographed the unsigned log, the sheet, and the ON air light. Then I logged a holdover. At 4:15 the station manager asked why Rex's mic was on my hours. I waited where the camera already was. If it is written, it can be applied to the person who wrote it.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The station manager can see Rex still ON with no sign-off at the start of my log.

social.video_title: He stayed live past sign-off into my board hours — Part 1/2
social.description: Community radio, a program sheet, and an ON light. I logged the holdover. Would you have photographed the log?

parts.text: Rex called it a set until the manager asked for the log. I printed the holdover, the photo, and the wall. He signed off. Rex set in his own hours and told DJs sets were always about optics. Optics is a word personalities use when an ON light exists. Board hours now have a second line: PERSONALITIES SIGN OFF. I keep 4–6. Rex logs. The studio finally sounds like a log, not a lease. I go back to being a person with a receipt. The second photo is for the person who will say they never saw the first.

social.description: Holdover log, signed-off mic, and a second line. Was a set ever my sheet?
